topic.title: Milk goes up in steps you will not fight
topic.claim: Milk is the one price you never argue about, which is exactly why it can go up Rs 4 in one step.
topic.behaviour: We spend weeks comparing a phone or a sale price. The litre of milk that arrives every morning gets a shrug and a paid-up monthly bill.
topic.mechanism: A daily purchase with no substitute gets no shopping around, so a price rise meets almost no resistance. People complain, then they pay, because the tea has to be made.
topic.group: Working households that run a monthly budget
topic.moment: You scroll through three sites to save Rs 500 on earphones, then pay the new milk price without reading the bill.

turn.believed: We are careful spenders who hunt for the best price.
turn.actually: We are careful only where there is a choice. Where there is none, the price just moves.

topic.feeling: Quietly squeezed, with nobody to argue with
topic.villain: A pricing model that sets rises on the things you cannot skip
topic.because: Dairies cite higher costs for fodder, cattle feed, packaging and transport. A product bought every single day passes those costs on with the least resistance.

proof.fact: Amul and Mother Dairy raised liquid milk prices by Rs 2 to 4 per litre, and Mother Dairy's hike was Rs 4 in a single step. Delhi consumers said earlier revisions were about Re 1 at a time.
October retail inflation was 6.09%, up from 5.5% in September, and food inflation was 8.94%.

topic.payoff: Make a list of the five things you buy every week without comparing. That is where your budget actually leaks.
topic.send_to: The friend who tracks every Swiggy coupon but never looks at the grocery bill
real_details: Consumers complained that prices are revised every few months, which makes monthly budgeting difficult.
Onions were ₹53.81 a kilo on 12 November against ₹26.91 a year earlier.
topic.news_peg: Amul and Mother Dairy raised milk prices from Thursday 12 November 2026, and retail inflation data released on 12 November showed 6.09% for October.
topic.why_now: Milk, onions and sugar all moved in the same month, and the budget feels it before the headline does.

score.why: We hunt for a Rs 500 saving on earphones and never question the milk bill; the list of things you never compare is a good test.

sources.fact: Amul and Mother Dairy raised liquid milk prices by Rs 2–4 per litre from 12 November 2026, citing higher fodder, cattle feed and packaging costs.
sources.stance: supports: the page gives the dairies' cost reasons (fodder, cattle feed ingredients, packaging film and fuel, uneven rainfall, higher payments to farmers). The fetched text did not mention transport, and it says nothing about consumers accepting the hike without resistance.
sources.excerpt: increased the prices of their liquid milk variants by Rs 2–4 per litre, effective 12 November. | green and dry fodder, cattle feed ingredients such as oil cake, maize and molasses | packaging film and fuel | low and uneven rainfall in Gujarat and several other parts of the country

sources.fact: Retail inflation rose to 6.09% in October 2026 from 5.54% in September, with food inflation at 8.94%, according to government data released 12 November.
sources.stance: neutral: it confirms the inflation figure and the rise in food prices. It does not discuss milk pricing or the dairies' stated reasons. I could not read the MoSPI release itself, because the PDF came back as unreadable binary.
sources.excerpt: India's retail inflation surged to 6.09 per cent in October, up from 5.54 per cent in September. | Government data released today (12 November) confirmed the breach. | Food inflation accelerated sharply to 8.94 per cent in October from 7.74 per cent in September.

cover.headline: We argue over every price except [the milk packet]
cover.sub: Which is exactly why milk can jump in one go.

paragraphs:
We fight over every price except milk. Which is why milk can jump in one go.
Swipe →
slides.why_swipe: Jump by how much, and why does nobody fight it?

paragraphs: Mother Dairy's latest hike was ₹4 a litre in a single step. Delhi buyers remember when revisions came about ₹1 at a time.
A bigger jump. And next morning the cold packet was still hanging in the bag on the door handle.
You check Amazon, Flipkart and Croma to save ₹500 on earbuds. You read reviews, wait for the sale, add the bank-card offer.
The monthly milk bill gets paid in one tap. The rate on it goes unread.
slides.why_swipe: So which one actually cost more?

paragraphs: A family of four easily goes through two litres a day. ₹4 more on each is ₹240 a month, close to ₹3,000 a year.
slides.why_swipe: If we're such careful spenders, how did this slip past?

paragraphs: We think we're careful spenders. We're careful only where we have options.
Earbuds come in fifty brands. The chai at home needs milk tomorrow, and the day after, and every day after that.
slides.why_swipe: Is the hike even unfair, then?

paragraphs: The dairies blame fodder, cattle feed and packaging. Fair.
But when costs go up, they land hardest on the thing bought every morning with nothing to swap it for. People grumble on the family WhatsApp group, then pay, because the tea has to be made.

If you run the house budget, you feel it before any headline does. You set the budget on the 1st. By the next revision, the milk line is already wrong. There's no sale to wait for, no one to argue with.
slides.why_swipe: So where is your month actually leaking?

paragraphs: Name the five things you buy every week without checking the price. Milk comes first.
That list leaks more of your month than any earbuds cart ever saved.

end.save: Read it again the next time you open three apps for one gadget.
end.send: Send to the friend who tracks every Swiggy coupon but never looks at the grocery bill.

draft.alt_text: An eight-slide text post arguing that Indians compare prices hard on gadgets but never on milk, which lets a dairy raise milk by ₹4 a litre in one step. It works out that the hike costs a two-litre household about ₹240 a month, more than a one-time ₹500 saving on earbuds. It accepts the dairies' stated fodder, feed and packaging costs, argues that cost rises land hardest on daily items with no substitute, and ends by asking readers to name the five weekly items they buy without checking the price.

claims.text: Mother Dairy's latest hike was ₹4 a litre in a single step.
Delhi buyers remember earlier revisions coming about ₹1 at a time.
₹4 more on two litres a day is ₹240 a month, close to ₹3,000 a year.
claims.derived_from: ₹4 x 2 litres x 30 days = ₹240 a month; ₹240 x 12 = ₹2,880 a year
